annotations.title: Add a variant to a step

description: Add another version of a step's message, to split the leads between them and see which works better. The step's own words are the original; a step holds up to 4 variants besides it, each live at once. Each lead draws one arm for the step, once, in proportion to the weights (the original's is the step's `weight`, a variant's defaults to 50), and keeps it: the same lead always gets the same arm. `name` left out is the next free letter (B, C, ...); a name is unique among the live variants, so archiving one frees it. `subject` left out or blank uses the step's. A step that replies in the thread (any step after the first with `threadReply`) keeps the thread's subject: a variant there changes the message only, and a subject on one answers 400 `variantSubjectThreading`. Subject and bodies are Liquid templates (`{{ first_name }}`, `{{ contact["Company size"] }}`, `{% if company %}`) with spintax (`{Hi|Hello}`) after them. One that does not parse answers 400 `templateInvalid`, with `details` naming each part and its line and column. Nothing is saved. Words in double brackets ([[like this]]) are a template's blanks: a save that still holds one answers 400 `stepBlank`, naming it. To start from words that already exist (list_campaign_templates, or get_saved_reply), copy them in as `bodyText`, and send `bodyHtml: ""` too when the step already has a formatted part, since most mail apps show that part. Adding a variant adds to what the campaign sends. On a running campaign, a change that adds to what it sends or to whom also needs the `send` permission, and makes the caller its approver. Through an API key an owner limited, the key's limits must cover the campaign, every mailbox it sends from and outreach, or it answers 403 with `details.scope` naming the limit. A change that only takes something out needs none of that.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.
